crossRefs.note: Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place, where you may see them. You shall see just part of them, and…
God is not a man, that he should lie, nor a son of man, that he should repent. Has he said, and will he not do it? Or…
Behold, I have received a command to bless. He has blessed, and I can’t reverse it.
But he stands alone, and who can oppose him? What his soul desires, even that he does.
There are many plans in a man’s heart, but Yahweh’s counsel will prevail.
There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against Yahweh.
For Yahweh of Armies has planned, and who can stop it? His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?”
I declare the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that are not yet done. I say: My counsel will…
I call a ravenous bird from the east, the man of my counsel from a far country. Yes, I have spoken. I will also bring…
“For I, Yahweh, don’t change; therefore you, sons of Jacob, are not consumed.
For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.

people.name: Balaam
people.line: A prophet hired to curse Israel but blessed them instead.

people.name: Balak
people.line: King of Moab who hired Balaam to curse Israel.

translations.web: Balak said to Balaam, “Come now, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will please God that you may curse them for me from there.”
translations.bsb: “Please come,” said Balak, “I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God that you curse them for me from there.”
translations.kjv: And Balak said unto Balaam, Come, I pray thee, I will bring thee unto another place; peradventure it will please God that thou mayest curse
translations.asv: And Balak said unto Balaam, Come now, I will take thee unto another place; peradventure it will please God that thou mayest curse me them from thence.
